verdicts.reason: Every evidence element checks out: run_pr174_sw_ray_tracer.py:73 defaults the consumer scan to (REPO/'htt', REPO/'scripts'), while pr174_spec.yaml's no_likelihood_firewall.enforcement promises a scan of "every non-test production module" with any hit a hard card failure. Non-test production Python outside the scanned roots demonstrably exists (16 tracked files in dl_pipeline/scripts/ incl. fetch.py, plus .agent-harness/scripts/; 159 tracked .py files outside htt/, scripts/, tests/ — though the finding's mention of formal_pr1xx is a minor overstatement since those dirs contain Lean, not Python). The guard test (test_pr_174...py:88,114) calls firewall_scan() with the same defaults, so both enforcement surfaces are two-root. Independent repo-wide grep for 'pr174_sw_ray_tracer' found only the runner and the test file, confirming no actual production consumer exists — the terminal SW_ONLY_MECHANICS_CONSISTENT_WITH_CLOSED_FORM is factually unaffected, which correctly calibrates severity at P1 (enforcement scope weaker than registered label; card firewall.pass=true asserts a repo-wide property verified only over two roots) rather than P0.

All evidence verified: pr169_closeout_review_receipt.json:21 carries the past-tense caveat "at PR-174 close the PR-169 scanner ... were deterministically refreshed" plus three updated hashes in the uncommitted working-tree diff; pr_status.yaml line 134 shows in_progress: PR-174; docs/PR_DELTAS/pr-174.md does not exist; git status shows the receipt modified-uncommitted alongside six untracked PR-174 artifacts, and HEAD (208dddcb) is a mid-PR amend commit, not a close. The tracked record asserts a close-time event that has not occurred and is honest only if these edits land atomically in the close commit. P2 severity is appropriate (record-honesty/atomicity hazard, does not invalidate the PR-174 result).

docs/PR_DELTAS/pr-174.md does not exist; the backlog card requires it (pr_backlog.yaml:4719, minor drift from claimed :4716); the convention is enforced in practice — 135 pr-NNN.md delta docs exist and closing commits for neighboring PRs (ff2b9c14 pr-176.md, e5dabc2a pr-179.md) ship the delta doc in the closing commit itself; PR-174 files are still untracked with no closing commit, so the doc must be authored before it. P1 severity is correct.

Reproduced the live demo exactly: firewall_scan() (run_pr174_sw_ray_tracer.py:63-71) returned pass=True with forbidden_import_hits=[] on a module importing healpy via line-continuation, __import__('healpy'), and importlib.import_module('bass'+'.los') — the line-based startswith('import '/'from ') filter plus substring blacklist misses all three vectors. grep confirms allowed_imports (pr174_spec.yaml:147) is referenced by zero code — the whitelist is entirely unenforced, contradicting the spec's "either hit is a hard failure" enforcement prose (spec:153). The guard test only exercises the trivially detectable 'from bass.los import anything' form. P2 severity is correct: the shipped module's actual imports (module lines 18-27) are all whitelisted, so the committed card is not invalidated — this is a mechanism weakness, not an existing violation.

All evidence verified: runner line 73 scans only REPO/htt + REPO/scripts while spec lines 150-153 claim it "scans every non-test production module"; directory census reproduced exactly (dl_pipeline 21, research_gates 44, prep06 21, pr07_repair_execution_pack 48, sage 7 .py files unscanned); the rel.startswith('tests/') branch at line 81 can never match under either default roots (rel begins htt/ or scripts/) or test-injected out-of-repo roots (rel is absolute) — dead code as claimed; the guard test uses the same default-root scan with only a synthetic fake_root for injection demos, so nothing compensates. Repo-wide grep confirms zero real consumers exist (only the runner and test file reference the module), so production_consumers=[] is factually correct today — consistent with the finding's parenthetical and its P2 (guard-weaker-than-spec, no live violation) severity.

Verified: pr174_sw_ray_tracer.py:198 leggauss nodes/weights feed every recovered_alm float byte-embedded in pr174_result_card.json (incl. cancellation residues ~1e-24), runner --check is an exact byte compare (run_pr174_sw_ray_tracer.py:190), numpy's leggauss uses LAPACK eigvalsh + Newton with no cross-version bit-identity guarantee, both PR-174 cards contain zero runtime_environment fields while PR-169 (run_pr169_unsigned_leakage.py:287-290) records one, and venv numpy 2.5.0 is unpinned in any PR-174 artifact. Only nuance: PR-169 also omits numpy version, but its scalars are exact Fractions so the omission is load-bearing only for PR-174; does not refute the finding. P2 severity appropriate.

Reproduced exactly: with n_phi=64 (config line 45), probe_dirs = dirs[::64] (pr174_sw_ray_tracer.py:324) selects only indices with k % 64 == 0, which by the grid construction (lines 201, 204: cos_t repeated over n_phi, phis tiled) all have phi=0; a live run gives max |y| = 0.0 over the 32 grid probes and confirms no probe in the 35-ray set (32 grid + eye(3)) mixes y with another component — the y-axis appears only as a pure axis probe. The spec's 'every sampled ray' criterion (pr174_spec.yaml:123) is thus met by an x-z-plane-only mixed subset. Severity P2 is correct: the RK4 update (lines 130-143) is component-wise diagonal with a direction-independent coefficient, so a y-sector bug can only enter via b_vector[1], which is exercised by the pure y-axis probe and by the full-sky 2048-ray quadrupole check (a22 depends on dbeta_x - dbeta_y, b_y = -0.5e-6 distinct), so the gap weakens but does not blind the battery.

Verified: (1) E(-n)=E(n) exactly for ANY coefficient/stages because dq/ds=-c_i(s)q_i is linear and direction-independent (pr174_sw_ray_tracer.py:110-144); empirically sign-flip, Euler, and a garbage coefficient all leave odd_ell power at roundoff (1e-22..1e-28) while ray_level/quadrupole_match fail. (2) a00≡0 by the shared-weights normalization identity (lines 286-304); holds even with randomly broken weights (a00=-1.7e-16); card a00=7.18e-16 is pure roundoff. (3) The only odd_ell_parity mutant (MUT-174-PARITY) works solely through the battery-only map_mutation hook (lines 311, 357-358, 429), and — stronger than claimed — NO mutant targets monopole_dipole_residual at all. Minor caveat: the absolute phrase 'incapable of failing for any tracer defect' is slightly overstated — a quadrupole-annihilating defect (MUT-174-ISO) trips both checks via denominator collapse of the odd/quad and residual/quad ratios — but even then ray_level and quadrupole_match also fire, so the checks contribute zero independent discrimination, which is the finding's substantive point. P2 severity appropriate.

All cited evidence verified in htt/src/common/pr174_sw_ray_tracer.py: _trace_broken_prediction (lines 439-443) only adds 1e-6 to delta_beta[2] inside the a20 term of the prediction dict, the same prediction-override channel as _perturbed_prediction (lines 433-436), and both mutants are registered against the same quadrupole_match guard (lines 463-470) — confirmed killed by that single guard in docs/generated/pr174_mutation_report.json. Independent rederivation confirms the shipped a20 = -2*sqrt(pi/5)*delta_beta_z (line 187) is the trace-reduced form of the general deviatoric a20 = -2*sqrt(pi/5)*(delta_beta_z - tau/3); no mutant probes the tau/3 term, no mutant feeds a trace-violating b_vector through the tracer/map, and the config.validate trace gate (lines 76-78) is exercised by no mutant and no test (zero occurrences of validate in tests/pr_cards/test_pr_174_*.py). The spec's MUT-174-TRACE description ("break the sum_i B_i = 0 trace condition in the prediction path", pr174_spec.yaml line 172) is therefore not implemented as described: the battery has two mutants covering one channel and zero coverage of the real sum(B_i)=0 pathway. P2 severity is correct — coverage overstatement, not invalidation of the mechanics result.
